title: Ada and the Ember
premise: When the valley's border wards collapse and the stars go dark, Silas Eastwick discovers her debt-bound servitude was a lie: her own soul was sold to the Ember Court beneath the mountain, and its theft is why magic cannot follow her. Guided by Ada, a fox-spirited ember-keeper who remembers what Silas has forgotten, she descends into the court to steal herself back before the starless long winter seals the mountain forever. The court's magistrate offers her freedom at the price of another soul — a child debtor like she once was. Silas refuses, shatters the ledger that binds all debtors, and returns to the valley with no magic but her name restored, as the first stars relight.
about_author: Quentin Thornbury is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing legal documents and now writes fantasies about paperwork gone wrong in magical places. They live near a real valley where, they insist, nothing supernatural has ever happened on record.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Silas copies ledgers in the temple of a valley where magic cannot follow, dreaming of a world she's never seen. On the night the wards fall and every star vanishes, a burning fox spirit named Ada crashes through her window demanding to know why Silas casts no shadow-magic. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: restless longing curdling into fear as the safe, dull valley breaks open.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Owes
chapters.summary: Ada leads Silas to the ruined border shrine, where a scorched contract reveals the truth: Silas's soul was sold to the Ember Court to pay her mother's debts, leaving her hollow enough that magic slides off her. The long winter begins falling; travelers freeze mid-road. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: identity shattered — she was never free, only empty — hardening into furious resolve to descend the mountain.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: In the Ember Court, a glittering underworld lit by stolen souls, Magistrate Veyne offers Silas a bargain: walk free if she signs over the soul of a child debtor in her place. Silas wavers — freedom, warmth, a whole self — while Ada burns dimmer each hour outside the court's reach. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: temptation at its peak, power offered as corruption, until she sees the child's eyes and understands what she almost becomes.

chapters.title: Ash and First Light
chapters.summary: Silas refuses the bargain and seizes the master ledger, tearing it apart as the court erupts; Ada ignites fully, and the freed souls rise through the mountain like sparks returning skyward. Escaping as winter cracks, Silas regains her soul — and chooses justice outside any law by freeing every debtor, not just herself. In the valley, the first star relights. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: costly triumph, grief for what was lost, quiet wholeness at last.
